DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
## Summary

The recommendation should not go ahead. By the paper's own trial results, ParcelLine **fails two of the four stated requirements**. Its on-time rate was 93.1% against the 95% minimum, and its damage rate was 0.9% against the 0.5% maximum. Once damage and loss are costed at the paper's own £48 per incident, it becomes the **most expensive** carrier, not the cheapest. Its lower "where is my order?" contact rate cannot be credited to its app, because only ParcelLine's parcels carried the new delivery-day text message for half the trial.

The trial itself is well designed. Random allocation of about 5,000 parcels per carrier is a fair basis for comparison, and its results point clearly to SwiftDrop or Meridian.

## What I checked

The price arithmetic is correct:
- **Cost per parcel at the 70/30 mix:** SwiftDrop £3.55, ParcelLine £3.48, Meridian £3.63.
- **Monthly cost:** £149,100, £146,160 and £152,460.
- **ParcelLine's price advantage:** £2,940 and £6,300 a month, which is £35,280 and £75,600 a year.
- **The contact saving:** 5 fewer contacts per 1,000 parcels × 42 × £3.20 = £672 a month.

## Errors

**1. ParcelLine did not meet the service requirements.** Section 3 says on-time delivery "was above 95% for all three carriers." Table 1 shows ParcelLine at **93.1%**. Its damage rate of **0.9%** is almost double the 0.5% maximum in section 2. SwiftDrop and Meridian meet all four requirements.

These are not small-sample effects. With about 5,000 parcels each:
- **On-time:** the 3-point gap between ParcelLine and SwiftDrop is several times the sampling error.
- **Damage:** about 45 damaged parcels against about 20.

The lost-parcel figures, by contrast, rest on a handful of parcels per carrier and shouldn't carry much weight.

**2. ParcelLine is the most expensive once damage and loss are included.** Section 2 costs each damaged or lost parcel at £48, but section 4 leaves this out. Including it, at 42,000 parcels a month:

| Carrier | Delivery cost | Damage + loss rate | Damage + loss cost | Total per month |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £149,100 | 0.43% | £8,669 | **£157,769** |
| ParcelLine | £146,160 | 0.98% | £19,757 | **£165,917** |
| Meridian | £152,460 | 0.32% | £6,451 | **£158,911** |

On this basis, ParcelLine costs about **£8,100 a month more than SwiftDrop**, roughly £98,000 a year, and about £7,000 a month more than Meridian. Even crediting its full contact saving of £672 a month, it remains about £7,500 a month dearer than SwiftDrop. This also leaves out the effect of damage on one-star reviews, which the paper says matters commercially.

**3. The contact reduction has two possible causes.** From 1 May, ParcelLine's parcels carried the new proactive delivery-day text message, and the other carriers' parcels didn't. That covers half the trial. The text message alone could explain fewer "where is my order?" contacts. It's notable that ParcelLine had the most late parcels yet the fewest of these contacts, which fits the text message explanation.

The trial data can partly separate the two causes. Compare ParcelLine's contact rate in April, before the texts, with the other carriers in April. The proactive text is Larkspur's own service, so once rolled out it should reduce contacts whichever carrier is chosen.

## Other points

- **Peak season.** The contract starts in October, so it covers peak trading in November and December. The trial ran in April and May. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers of a similar size. ParcelLine's references are mainly lighter fashion parcels. That gap matters given that 30% of parcels are 2–10 kg lamps, mirrors and furniture.
- **Damage by weight band.** Break damage down by weight for each carrier. If ParcelLine's damage is concentrated in heavier items, that would confirm the peak-season concern.
- **Contract term.** The 12-month term is not a ParcelLine advantage. SwiftDrop offers the same. Only Meridian requires 24 months.

## Settled and open

**Settled:**
- ParcelLine failed the on-time and damage requirements in the trial;
- including damage and loss, it is the most expensive option;
- the contact reduction can't be attributed to its app.

**Open:**
- **SwiftDrop or Meridian.** SwiftDrop is about £1,100 a month cheaper on total cost, roughly £13,700 a year, and offers a 12-month term. Meridian has the best service on every measure but needs a 24-month commitment. This is a judgement call for the business. A useful input is how much one-star reviews from damage cost beyond the £48 per incident.
- **How much the text message reduces contacts.** The April versus May comparison above will give a first answer, and measuring after roll-out to all carriers will settle it.

## Recommendation

Do not award the contract to ParcelLine. Choose between SwiftDrop and Meridian:
- **SwiftDrop** is the default: lowest total cost, meets every requirement, 12-month term, peak experience.
- **Meridian** is worth choosing if service quality and fewer damaged parcels outweigh about £14,000 a year and the 24-month term.

Roll out the proactive delivery-day text to all parcels, whichever carrier is chosen.
